newsitem.title: USA: Ariz. Navajo 750 MW coal-fired unit said to shut.
newsitem.headline: Ariz. Navajo 750 MW coal-fired unit said to shut.

text.p: The 750 megawatt (MW) unit 1 at the Navajo coal-fired power plant near Page, Ariz., was shut over the weekend for unplanned repairs, sources familiar with the plant's operations said Monday.
Some sources said it was expected back on-line by Wednesday.
The plant's 750 MW unit 3 continues to undergo testing after being shut for scheduled maintenance since late February.
The Navajo plant is operated by Salt River Project, which holds a 21.8percent equity stak in the plant.
Other owners include the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation, Los Angeles Department of Water and Power, Arizona Public Service Co, Nevada Power Co and Tucson Electric Power Co.
